decisions.sample: one small sub-directory per major language family (TS, Rust, Ruby, Scala) so indexing completes in seconds per entry — the proof is the dry-run-no-mutation + no-corruption contract, not exhaustive coverage
decisions.dryRun: every refactor uses dryRun:true; the on-disk file content is compared byte-for-byte before vs after to prove zero writes
decisions.corruption: symbol counts are compared pre- vs post-dry-run reindex; any divergence is a recorded failure, not hidden

limitations: Only a small sub-directory per repo is indexed (full 29-repo indexing is hours-long); broader coverage is.
A sub-directory with no resolvable symbol is skipped (recorded, not failed).

Refactor is UNAVAILABLE for Erlang: its grammar yields zero identifier occurrences, so the engine refuses by name rather than reporting a rename it cannot perform (D3/M71; measured with script/m71/diagnose-erlang-refactor.ts). The Erlang leg asserts that refusal instead of pretending the dry-run renamed something.
